years with a set of agreed Policy Aims and an accompanying Delivery
Plan. In 2023 all AONBs were rebranded as National Landscapes to
better reflect their national importance.

content:
RESOLVED
that
 

That the Cabinet recommend to Full Council that
it:

a)   
Approves the Building a Better Future Plan (Appendix
A) for submission to the Secretary of State for Housing,
Communities and Local Government;

Following a), that Cabinet:

b)   
Approves the consultation on the Building a Better
Future Plan (Appendix A) from 20 July 2026 to 9 September 2026
following the Consultation Plan set out in Appendix B;

 

c)    
Delegates authority to the Strategic Director of
Growth and Place, following consultation with the Cabinet Lead for
Coastal, Coastal Communities & Local Plan, to make any
necessary amendments to the Building a Better Future Plan (Appendix
A) and its supporting documents prior to the consultation. These
shall be limited to the inclusion of a contents page and page
numbers, the key diagram, factual and data updates, correction of
minor errors, typographical errors and other minor changes that do
not change the meaning of the material;
 

d)   
Delegates authority to the Strategic Director for
Growth and Place, following consultation with the Cabinet Lead for
Coastal, Coastal Communities & Local Plan, to prepare a report,
which forms one of the documents to submit to the Secretary of
State for Housing, Communities and Local Government, noting the
number of representations made through the consultation and a
summary of the main issues raised;
 

e)   
Delegates authority to the Strategic Director for
Growth and Place, following consultation with the Cabinet Lead for
Coastal, Coastal Communities & Local Plan, to submit to the
Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government
the Building a Better Future Plan (Appendix A, as may be modified
by recommendation c) and the necessary supporting documentation for
examination;

Delegates authority to the Strategic Director for
Growth and Place, following consultation with the Cabinet Lead for
Coastal, Coastal Communities & Local Plan, to undertake
consultation on any ‘main modifications’ or other
matters which the Inspector for the examination of the Building a
Better Future Plan requests.

fuel costs for the Contractor. The NEC4 Term Service Contract
includes a Compensation Event clause that excludes events that
neither party could prevent, and that an experienced contractor
would have judged to have such a small chance of occurring that it

warning to HBC of a potential impact.

records provided by the contractor, together with delivery notes to
the work site, have been inspected to validate the claim value of
£9,503.10.

content:
The
variable fees for the Stray Dogs and Animal Licensing services were
omitted from the documents presented to Overview and Scrutiny
Committee, and the Fees and Charges Schedule for 2026/27 agreed by
Cabinet on 3 December 2025.
 
The
variable fees for the Stray Dogs and Animal Licensing services were
omitted from the documents presented to Overview and Scrutiny
Committee, and the Fees and Charges Schedule for 2026/27 agreed by
Cabinet on 3 December 2025 due to an administrative error caused by
the values being a range rather than a fixed sum.
 

Approval
of the following variable fees for the animal welfare and licensing
services, which were omitted in error from the Fees and Charges
Schedule for 2026/27 agreed by Cabinet on 3 December
2025.
 
•
Stray Dogs: Emergency medical treatment of dogs in care of the
Council (recovery of costs)

o 2026/27 Fee: Variable
 
•
Animal Licensing: Zoo applications (charged at hourly rate, will
include interim and full inspections and work undertaken to
reinspection, excludes vet inspections which will be recharged
separately at cost price)

o 2026/27 Fee: Variable
 
•
Animal Licensing: Any variation or amendment to licenses (£30
minimum + £25.50 per hour for additional work as
agreed)

o 2026/27 Fee: Variable •
 
Animal
Licensing: Primate applications (charged at hourly rate, interim
and full inspections and work undertaken to reinspection, excludes
vet inspections which will be recharged separately at cost
price)

o 2026/27 Fee: Variable
 
Fees for these services are cost-neutral,
meaning that they are set on a cost recovery basis only. Charging
these fees is essential to fund the delivery of these statutory
functions.
topline: The Cllr Richard Brown has decided to set variable fees for Stray Dogs and Animal Licensing services to fund statutory functions.

purpose:
Beach
replenishment is needed to prevent flooding of residential homes at
Eastoke Frontage area.
content:
Beach
replenishment is needed to prevent flooding of residential homes at
Eastoke Frontage area.
 

The
Eastoke frontage at Hayling Island
suffered significant erosion between 1st December and
7th December 2025. Bays 27, 28, 29, and 30 were severely
depleted, increasing the risk of flooding to properties that are
adjacent to the promenade. To maintain protection through to the
next planned recycling the beach needs to be re-built as far as
possible Material will be pushed back from the promenade as well as
brought in from where it naturally builds up by Coast Guard
revetment to support these areas.
 
The
Council has a Term Service Contract with provision for emergency
response with Les Searle Plant Hire Ltd.  And they were mobilised to undertake emergency
beach replenishment works. The operation is scheduled to take place
over 5 days, from 9 to 15 December 2025, at an estimated cost of
approximately £30,000.
topline: The Strategic Director, Coastal Partnerships has decided to approve recommendations for beach replenishment to prevent flooding of residential homes at Eastoke Frontage area

A decision

with East Hampshire District Council (EHDC) for the provision of
Building Control Services. Whilst Cabinet made the decision in
September to move the service to the BCP from 17 October 2025, this
decision seeks to also continue the IAA with East Hampshire
District Council for a further month to enable continued access to
IDOX Cloud whilst the IT contractor seeks to finalise separating
the Havant and East Hampshire data.
 

Timescales
for removing Havant’s data from East Hampshire’s IDOX
Cloud system to be part of the BCP has taken longer than
anticipated.  Continued access to the
data is essential for business continuity and the IAA provides
appropriate data sharing protocols.
 

The
preferred option of separating the data by 17 October 2025 has not
been achievable.

purpose:

paragraph 20. ‘The Cabinet (Executive) Functions
content:
Cabinet
Lead Delegated Decision taken pursuant to Part Two, Section D
paragraph 20. ‘The Cabinet (Executive) Functions
 


1.               
THE DECISION:
 
To spend
the funding on
 
·      
Rent Arrears £126,632.50 – This option
allows us to reach many in need and we have statistics from the
Housing providers of those in need of assistance with arrears. It
will prevent homelessness for over 50 tenants that would then
require us to house them at a large cost to the Council. It will
support others to move to a more affordable and sustainable
tenancy.
·      
Bulk food purchase and the hygiene boxes
£20,000 – This will reach across the whole Borough and
will reach some of those vulnerable people that may otherwise be
missed as not on other benefits but are in need of
support.
 
         
 

2.               
REASONS FOR DECISION:
 
The rent
arrears option allows for the Council to prevent the homelessness
of a potential 50 residents that would then present homeless to the
Council and need more funding and support. It will enable more
residents to move to a more sustainable accommodation for them
giving them the ability to remain housed and in a more affordable
property.
 
 

Food vouchers were considered but the amount of
funding that each eligible individual would potentially receive was
minimal and not have as great an impact as the options
chosen 
 
White good were
considered, however the administration of this is difficult and
there was no understanding of the need for
this in the Borough.
topline: The Cabinet Lead for Commercial has decided to allocate funding for rent arrears and bulk food purchase to prevent homelessness and support vulnerable residents in need.
